tasks.q: Which of these count as personal data? Select all that apply.
opts: Your home postcode with your date of birth
correct: Your home postcode with your date of birth
tasks.fb: If it can be traced back to a person, it is personal data.

tasks.q: Why is data about what you look at so valuable to advertisers?
a: It predicts what you are likely to buy, so adverts can be aimed precisely
tasks.fb: Attention is the product being sold.

a: Building a picture of someone from many small pieces of collected data
tasks.fb: Individually harmless facts can add up to something very personal.

tasks.q: A torch app asks for access to your contacts. What is the concern?
a: It doesn't need contacts to work, so the data is likely being collected to sell or profile
Torches use a lot of battery
It is illegal to have a torch app
tasks.fb: Ask what a feature genuinely needs.

tasks.q: Which of these is closest to meaningful consent?
a: A short, clear choice where refusing is as easy as accepting
A 12,000-word policy with an Accept button
A banner with only one button
Consent assumed by continuing to scroll
tasks.fb: If refusing is hard, it isn't freely given.

tasks.q: Why does the law treat children's data more carefully?
a: Children are less able to understand what they are agreeing to
tasks.fb: That's why services aimed at children have stricter rules.

tasks.q: Is each point a benefit of collecting data, or a risk?
items: Your bank spots a fraudulent payment
A leaked database exposes millions of addresses
A map app routes you around traffic
An insurer charges more based on a profile
Health researchers spot a disease pattern early
An employer searches your posts from years ago
tasks.fb: A good answer admits the benefits and then weighs them against the risks.

tasks.q: Which is the best exam sentence about smart speakers?
a: They make information hands free, but a microphone in every room is a serious privacy risk if recordings are stored or leaked

tasks.q: Why is collecting less data a privacy protection?
a: Data that was never collected cannot leak, be sold or be misused
tasks.fb: Data minimisation is the cheapest protection there is.

tasks.q: Why can a privacy breach be worse than a stolen bank card?
a: A card can be replaced, but a medical record or a home address cannot be made private again

tasks.q: A school installs software that logs every website pupils visit, at school and at home on school laptops. How is each group affected?

stakeholders.name: Pupils at risk of harm online

tasks.fb: Safeguarding is a real benefit; monitoring a pupil's home use is a real intrusion. Both belong in the answer.
tasks.title: School monitoring: who is affected?

a: Monitoring is defensible at school, but home use should be excluded unless parents are told exactly what is recorded
Schools should decide without telling anyone
tasks.fb: A limit, with the reason it falls there.

tasks.q: How would you classify each practice?
items: A map app using your location while you navigate
A bank checking a payment against your usual pattern
A shop's app tracking which aisles you walk down
A fitness app sharing your heart data with an insurer
A game collecting your contacts list
A school reading pupils' personal messages
An advertiser building a profile from sites you visit
tasks.fb: There is no single right line, but you must be able to justify where you put it.

info.title: The price of free
info.text: If a service is free, the running costs are usually paid for by advertising, and advertising is paid for by what is known about you.

info.title: Anonymous isn't
info.text: Studies have shown that a few 'anonymous' details, such as postcode, date of birth and sex, identify most people uniquely.

info.title: Metadata matters
info.text: Who you called and when can reveal more than the conversation itself: a call to a clinic followed by a call to a relative tells a story.

info.title: Dark patterns
info.text: Designs that make accepting easy and refusing hard have a name, and regulators have started fining companies for them.

info.title: Right to be forgotten
info.text: In the UK and EU you can ask for personal data to be deleted in many circumstances, though not where there's a legal reason to keep it.

info.title: Check your settings
info.text: Every phone has a screen listing which apps have location, microphone and camera access. Most people are surprised by it.
